---
title: "Load the bundled demo dataset"
---

## Load the bundled demo dataset {.unnumbered}


### Description

Returns a small, deterministic genomic dataset bundled with the package,
intended for examples, vignettes, and tests.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>load_data(size = c("small", "large"))
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="size">size</code></td>
<td>
character, either <code>"small"</code> (default) or <code>"large"</code>.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

Two scales are bundled: <code>size = "large"</code> (n=200, p=500,
n_qtl=20) and <code>size = "small"</code> (default; n=100, p=50, n_qtl=5) that run
during <code>R CMD check --examples</code>.
Both have the same family structure (10 full-sib families) and the
same 12-field shape.

The data simulates a small breeding-style population: 10 full-sib
families (each from one sire-dam founder pair). The founders are kept in
the pedigree only (no genotype, no phenotype). A within-family 80/20
train/test split is bundled so every test individual has its full-sibs in
training.



### Value

A list with the following elements (dimensions shown for
<code>size = "large"</code> / <code>size = "small"</code>):


<dl>
<dt><code>snp</code></dt><dd>Integer matrix $n \times p$ of biallelic SNP
dosages (values <code>0/1/2</code>). Rownames are individual IDs
<code>IND001..INDn</code>; colnames are <code>SNP001..SNPp</code>.
Dimensions: 200 x 500 (large) / 100 x 50 (small).
</dd>
<dt><code>mh</code></dt><dd>Integer matrix $n \times (2 \cdot n_{blocks})$ of
microhaplotype allele codes. Columns alternate strand 1 / strand 2
per block. The <code>attr(mh, "block_id")</code> attribute maps each column
to its block. Consumable directly by
<code>construct_wah_matrix()</code>. Dimensions: 200 x 500 with 250
blocks (large) / 100 x 50 with 25 blocks (small).
</dd>
<dt><code>allele_freq</code></dt><dd>List with parallel vectors
<code>haplotype</code>, <code>allele</code>, <code>freq</code> &ndash; the training-style
allele frequency table required by
<code>construct_wah_matrix(hap, block_id, allele_freq)</code>
when no <code>reference_structure</code> is supplied. Pre-computed from
the full bundled <code>mh</code> matrix.
</dd>
<dt><code>pheno</code></dt><dd>Data frame with <code>n</code> rows. Columns: <code>id</code>,
<code>sex</code> (factor F/M, balanced 50/50),
<code>y_cont_qtl_snp</code>, <code>y_cont_qtl_mh</code> (continuous traits under
two QTL architectures), <code>y_bin_qtl_snp</code>, <code>y_bin_qtl_mh</code>
(binary traits, threshold at median), <code>tbv_qtl_snp</code>,
<code>tbv_qtl_mh</code> (true breeding values).
</dd>
<dt><code>pedigree</code></dt><dd>Data frame with 220 (large) or 120 (small) rows:
10 sire founders + 10 dam founders (all NA parents) plus the
offspring with their sire/dam recorded. Columns: <code>id</code>,
<code>sire</code>, <code>dam</code>.
</dd>
<dt><code>qtl</code></dt><dd>List with <code>snp_idx</code>, <code>mh_idx</code>,
<code>effects_snp</code>, <code>effects_mh</code> (each length 20 for large, 5
for small; effects drawn from <code>rnorm</code>, unit-normalised).
</dd>
<dt><code>meta</code></dt><dd>List with <code>n</code>, <code>n_snp</code>, <code>n_blocks</code>,
<code>n_snp_per_block</code>, <code>n_qtl</code>, <code>n_families</code>,
<code>n_per_family</code>, <code>h2_target</code>, <code>sex_beta_snp</code>,
<code>sex_beta_mh</code>, <code>seed</code>, <code>split_seed</code>, <code>size</code>.
</dd>
<dt><code>family_id</code></dt><dd>Character vector length <code>n</code>, values
<code>fam_01..fam_10</code>.
</dd>
<dt><code>train_idx</code></dt><dd>Integer vector &ndash; row indices into
<code>snp</code>/<code>mh</code>/<code>pheno</code> for the training set. Length 160
(large) / 80 (small).
</dd>
<dt><code>test_idx</code></dt><dd>Integer vector &ndash; row indices for the test set.
Length 40 (large) / 20 (small). Every test individual has its
full-sibs in <code>train_idx</code>.
</dd>
<dt><code>map_snp</code></dt><dd>Data frame with one row per SNP. Columns
<code>SNP</code> (character), <code>CHROM</code> (integer 1..5), <code>POS</code>
(integer base-pair coordinate). Aligns 1-to-1 with the columns
of <code>snp</code> and with the design matrix from
<code>construct_snp_matrix()</code>. Ready to pass as the
<code>map</code> argument to <code>run_bayesr()</code> for GWAS.
Dimensions: 500 x 3 (large) / 50 x 3 (small).
</dd>
<dt><code>map_mh</code></dt><dd>Data frame with one row per MH block. Columns
<code>block_id</code> (character, matches
<code>unique(attr(mh, "block_id"))</code>), <code>chr</code>, <code>start_pos</code>,
<code>end_pos</code>, <code>n_snps</code> (integers). Schema matches
<code>microhaplotype_coordinates.csv</code> produced by the
<code>maspipeline</code> tool, so production pipelines can pass
<code>map_mh</code> unchanged into <code>run_bayesr()</code>.
Physical positions are synthetic (5 chromosomes, 100 kb intra-chr
SNP spacing, 1 Mb chr base offset); each block spans the two
consecutive SNPs that built it. Dimensions: 250 x 5 (large) /
25 x 5 (small).
</dd>
<dt><code>multigen</code></dt><dd>Nested list with the 3-generation
forward-prediction extension. Generated by
<code>tools/make_demo_data_3gen.R</code> (AlphaSimR + optiSel OCS) and
merged into this RDS. See <em>Multi-generation extension</em>
below for the sub-fields.
</dd>
</dl>



### On the microhaplotype representation in <code>d\$mh</code>

In production, microhaplotype genotypes are produced by the
<span class="pkg">maspipeline</span> preprocessing pipeline, where phasing with Beagle
or Shapeit, conversion to phased haplotype alleles, LD- or window-based
block discovery, then per-strand block encoding. The on-disk output is one
tab-separated file per chromosome with header

<pre>
ID         hap_1_1 hap_1_1 hap_1_2 hap_1_2 hap_2_1 hap_2_1 hap_2_2 hap_2_2 ...
IND00001        1       1       2       2       1       1       2       2 ...
IND00002        1       1       1       1       2       2       1       1 ...
</pre>
Each block contributes 4 columns: <code>hap_&lt;b&gt;_1 hap_&lt;b&gt;_1 hap_&lt;b&gt;_2 hap_&lt;b&gt;_2</code>
(the per-strand block name repeated twice, with per-SNP allele codes 1 or
2 inside). Block coordinates and allele frequencies live in companion
CSVs (e.g.
<code>mh_info_ld_haploblock_G0/stats/microhaplotype_coordinates.csv</code>).

The <code>d\$mh</code> stored here is a compact in-memory equivalent for
demos: instead of per-SNP allele codes, each strand of each block is
collapsed into a single integer haplotype id via a base-3 polynomial
encoding of its SNP alleles. Shape becomes $n \times (2 \cdot n_{blocks})$
(two columns per block, not four), and the per-block frequency table is
bundled as <code>d\$allele_freq</code>. Both representations encode the same
biological information; <code>d\$mh</code> skips the file-layout overhead and
the recomputation of allele frequencies.



### Multi-generation extension (<code>d\$multigen</code>)

For forward-prediction examples
(<code>examples/05_forward_prediction.R</code>), <code>d\$multigen</code> bundles a
3-generation breeding lineage:


<ul>
<li> Gen-1 phenotyped (training pool).

</li>
<li> Gen-2 produced by OCS selection on gen-1, one cohort per QTL
architecture (<code>gen2_snp</code>, <code>gen2_mh</code>).

</li>
<li> Gen-3 produced by OCS on gen-2, also per architecture
(<code>gen3_snp</code>, <code>gen3_mh</code>).

</li></ul>

Two evaluation scenarios are supported:


<dl>
<dt>Scenario A</dt><dd>Train on gen-1, predict gen-2. Use
<code>multigen\$reference_structure_gen1</code> when building
$W_{\alpha h}$ for the test cohort so columns align with
training.
</dd>
<dt>Scenario B</dt><dd>Train on gen-1 + gen-2 (per architecture), predict
gen-3. Use
<code>multigen\$reference_structure_gen1_gen2_snp</code> or
<code>multigen\$reference_structure_gen1_gen2_mh</code> accordingly.
</dd>
</dl>

Sub-fields under <code>d\$multigen</code>:


<dl>
<dt><code>gen1</code></dt><dd>List(<code>snp</code>, <code>mh</code>, <code>allele_freq</code>,
<code>pheno</code>, <code>sire_of</code>, <code>dam_of</code>). <code>pheno</code> carries
both <code>y_cont_qtl_snp</code> and <code>y_cont_qtl_mh</code> plus matching
<code>tbv_qtl_*</code> columns.
</dd>
<dt><code>gen2_snp</code>, <code>gen2_mh</code></dt><dd>Gen-2 cohort lists; same shape
as <code>gen1</code> but <code>pheno</code> only carries the
architecture-matching trait + <code>tbv_qtl_*_true</code> ground truth.
<code>allele_freq</code> is the gen-1 frequency table (Scenario A
invariant).
</dd>
<dt><code>gen3_snp</code>, <code>gen3_mh</code></dt><dd>Gen-3 cohort lists, same
pattern as gen-2; <code>allele_freq</code> is the gen-1+gen-2 combined
frequency table (Scenario B reference).
</dd>
<dt><code>reference_structure_gen1</code>,
<code>reference_structure_gen1_gen2_snp</code>,
<code>reference_structure_gen1_gen2_mh</code></dt><dd>Full return values of
<code>construct_wah_matrix()</code> on the corresponding training
set. Pass as <code>reference_structure</code> when building the test
$W_{\alpha h}$.
</dd>
<dt><code>qtl</code></dt><dd>List with <code>mh_idx</code>, <code>effects_mh</code>,
<code>beta_mh</code> (effect vector anchored to gen-1
$W_{\alpha h}$ columns), and three SNP centring-mean vectors
for Scenario A / B SNP centring.
</dd>
<dt><code>pedigree</code></dt><dd>Combined pedigree across founders + gen-1 +
two gen-2 cohorts + two gen-3 cohorts.
</dd>
<dt><code>ocs</code></dt><dd>Diagnostics for all four OCS calls
(current/target/realised average kinship and parent
contributions), nested as
<code>ocs\$&lt;arch&gt;\$&lt;gen1_to_gen2|gen2_to_gen3&gt;</code>.
</dd>
<dt><code>meta</code></dt><dd>Per-cohort sizes, realised $h^2$ per
generation, target $\Delta F$, seed, and
<code>AlphaSimR</code>/<code>optiSel</code>/<code>masbayes</code> versions used to
build the dataset.
</dd>
</dl>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masbayes")

d <- load_data()
str(d, max.level = 1)
dim(d$snp)
head(d$pheno)

# Smaller dataset for fast examples / unit tests:
d_small <- load_data("small")
dim(d_small$snp)

# Multi-generation extension: forward-prediction layout
d3 <- d$multigen
str(d3, max.level = 1)
dim(d3$gen1$mh); dim(d3$gen2_mh$mh); dim(d3$gen3_mh$mh)
# Scenario A: train gen-1, predict gen-2 (W_alpha-h aligned via gen-1 ref):
W_tr <- d3$reference_structure_gen1$W_ah
W_te <- construct_wah_matrix(
  d3$gen2_mh$mh, attr(d3$gen2_mh$mh, "block_id"),
  reference_structure = d3$reference_structure_gen1
)$W_ah




```
